transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~48 mins | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood CSM) -- Anika Strauss (Riverbend Head of ML), Marcus Leung (Riverbend Platform), Priya Kapoor (Riverbend Security)

Summary (auto): Renewal / expansion check-in. Discussed contract extension options, capacity uplift schedule, EU & APAC region activation, security docs, and a pilot/benchmark plan. Next steps captured.

Topics: contract term options; committed capacity + burst credits; dedicated vs hosted; latency targets (p95/p99); security & compliance artifacts; pilot benchmarks.

Action items (captured): see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for making time, um this is the quarterly renewal check-in for Riverbend — uh welcome, can you all hear me ok?
[00:06] Anika: yeah loud and clear, thanks Jordan. Marcus and Priya on from our side as well.
[00:10] Jordan: awesome. Quick agenda: run through renewal options, talk capacity uplift plan across EU & APAC, then Maya will walk through benchmark approach, Diego will cover security docs and handoffs. any additions?
[00:20] Marcus: maybe procurement timeline, we'd like to align that so we can avoid swim lanes later.
[00:24] Jordan: good call, we'll cover that during legal/proc section.
[00:28] Maya: i can start with the benchmark idea — it's, uh, fairly straightforward; we want to measure sustained throughput, KV cache hit effects, and p95 latencies with sequence mixes matching your traf — traffic. we'll run both hosted and dedicated variants so we can quantify cost/latency delta.
[00:44] Anika: that sounds right. for us, the key is that model responses for PII flows need to be on private infra. currently we use a mix: sensitive flows on our private VPC dedicated infra, general customer-facing features on hosted. we're evaluating consolidating more onto dedicated.
[01:02] Priya: and security is the crux — need SOC2 artifacts, network diagrams, KMS integration details, plus proof of separation for logs.
[01:10] Diego: yeah we have a security packet, i'll share the SOC2 report and a redacted network diagram. note that Redwood private deployments support both customer-managed KMS and HSM via partner integration, which you asked about earlier.
[01:22] Priya: Hm, ok, can you confirm key rotation policies? we've got mandated rotation windows.
[01:28] Maya: sure, we support rotation and can map to your KMS policies; i'll include a short note in the packet.
[01:33] Jordan: circling back to capacity: we prototyped your q2 load and saw a 2.3x spike in APAC evenings, right? Marcus, is that persistent?
[01:42] Marcus: yes, the evening batch has grown. our ask is: +30% committed in APAC by Q1, +20% EU to reduce p95 from 240ms to under 150ms for the top 10 endpoints.
[01:54] Jordan: ok good. we can do staged commit: month 1 add a reserved pool in APAC, month 3 EU pool activation. We'll propose burst credits for seasonal peaks to avoid overcommit.
[02:07] Anika: what's the delta on cost if we go dedicated versus hosted for those endpoints? rough numbers are fine now.
[02:13] Maya: rough rule of thumb: dedicated typically lowers per-token infra cost by ~20-35% when fully utilized, but you trade flexibility. for latency-sensitive endpoints dedicated also reduces variance because of pinned capacity; hosted with autoscale is cheaper for occasional bursts but p95 can be higher depending on seq lengths.
[02:30] Marcus: that's what we suspected. can you show a worked example?
[02:33] Maya: sure - example: assuming 5k qps steady at seq len 128, dedicated node mix gives p95 ~90-120ms; hosted at same qps but mixed arrival patterns p95 drifts to ~180-260ms. those are approximate, we need your traffic profile to tighten the estimate.
[02:48] Jordan: also mention the quantization profile — using int8 variants on dedicated often changes cost math; we can recommend model quantization for non-sensitive flows.
[02:56] Priya: we'll need to validate that quantized models meet our accuracy bar — Anika will own evals.
[03:02] Anika: yep we'll run a 2k sample through quantized set.
[03:06] Maya: perfect. on region activation, we recommend bringing EU first, then APAC because of certificate provisioning and customs for some onprem boxes — small operational lead time.
[03:16] Marcus: lead time? two to three weeks?
[03:18] Maya: typically 10-21 business days for full VPC private activation in a new region if networking (VPC peering/firewall, routes) is pre-approved; Dedicated reserved pools can be faster if it's a hosted region already in our infra.
[03:32] Marcus: ok. procurement wants dates so we can align budget, legal needs a contract amendment.
[03:37] Jordan: we'll provide a proposed amendment with options: 12-month term (base uplift + burst credits), and a 24-month term with price protection. which would you prefer to see?
[03:47] Anika: show both, but highlight the 12-month with staged ramp as our preferred. we want flexibility.
[03:52] Diego: i'll include a pricing worksheet and a simple graph showing unit economics by utilization.
[03:56] Priya: on compliance — do you retain logs by default? we need audit log retention controls and ability to filter by tenant.
[04:04] Diego: yes, we support token-level logs and retention policies; for private deployments you control retention and ELK ingestion. we'll surface the exact retention APIs.
[04:12] Anika: perfect. how about SSO & RBAC? our identity team will need SCIM and SAML, plus role-based access.
[04:19] Jordan: Redwood supports SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning; RBAC roles are configurable. i'll attach our SSO guide.
[04:25] Marcus: any compatibility issues with our Okta setup?
[04:27] Maya: None expected. Okta + SAML + SCIM is common; some customers add MFA checks. we'll test in the pilot.
[04:35] Anika: pilot — let's go into plan. we want a 24-hour throughput run and a shorter live ramp (4 hours) to simulate evening surge from EU and APAC.
[04:45] Maya: plan we propose: 24-hour synthetic run from EU egress, APAC egress, and US baseline; measure p50/p95/p99, error rate, and cost per 10k tokens. we'll also toggle KV cache on/off to measure delta.
[04:58] Marcus: can we run from our egress nodes? we want to test real network e2e.
[05:01] Maya: yes, we'll coordinate for IP allowlist; Marcus we'll need a list of IPs for whitelisting and a small test key.
[05:09] Marcus: noted, i'll collect those.
[05:11] Priya: for the benchmark, what's the expected overhead for logging? we don't want extra noise.
[05:16] Maya: minimal; we'll collect sampling traces and raw logs for the harness only; you can opt-out of any telemetry.
[05:22] Jordan: legal/proc next: Diego, can you summarize the timeline we discussed?
[05:27] Diego: sure. we'll send amendment by Oct 5. procurement reviews typically take 7-14 days at Riverbend per Marcus's note — so target signing by Oct 21 if no blockers. pilot kickoff tentatively Oct 12.
[05:40] Marcus: that works for budgeting, October quarter start.
[05:44] Anika: one more question — competitor pricing we've received is lower on per-token but doesn't include private deployment costs. can Redwood show TCO for 12 months vs competitor bids?
[05:56] Jordan: yes we'll include a TCO appendix comparing hosted-only competitor pricing vs Redwood dedicated + hybrid options. note that competitors often exclude KMS & private audit support which matter for you.
[06:07] Priya: ok thanks.
[06:09] [crosstalk]
[06:12] Maya: last tech note — we'll instrument a small canary traffic route for canary rollouts; helps with rollback if we see a quality regression during quantized model deployment.
[06:22] Anika: good, we need that.
[06:24] Jordan: wrapping up: actions are to share amendment, security pack, run the benchmark, and confirm procurement timeline. anything we missed?
[06:32] Marcus: just the IP allowlist + traffic profile - I'll send by Oct 3.
[06:36] Priya: i'll loop in legal and security folks and confirm review windows.
[06:39] Diego: i'll create the Confluence space and attach the SOC2 + network diagrams by Oct 4.
[06:44] Jordan: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot and send the docs.
[06:50] Anika: thanks all.
[06:52] Jordan: bye.

End of transcript.
